name: Nasal Dermoid Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Nasal Dermoid Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a midline nasal mass or swelling, often congenital
Identification of a nasal pit or sinus tract on the dorsum of the nose
Imaging evidence (CT or MRI) of a cystic lesion with or without intracranial extension
Histopathological confirmation showing dermoid cyst characteristics (keratinized epithelium, adnexal structures)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a midline nasal mass with sinus tract or pit plus imaging confirmation of cystic lesion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Intracranial extension must be ruled out due to surgical implications.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically present at birth or early infancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Nasal dorsal sinus tract or pit
pathognomonic.notes: May intermittently discharge keratinous or sebaceous material
searchTerms: pit or opening on top of nose
small hole or sinus on nasal bridge

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by imaging; may be asymptomatic initially

common.symptomName: Localized tenderness or swelling over nasal bridge
common.notes: Often due to inflammation or infection

common.symptomName: Recurrent local infection or abscess formation

common.notes: Due to mass effect of cyst

common.symptomName: Discharge of sebaceous or keratinous material from sinus opening
searchTerms: pus or oily discharge from nose pit
sebum or keratin leaking from nasal opening
pain due to cyst inside skull
head pain caused by intracranial cyst

occasional.symptomName: Palpable subcutaneous tract extending toward nasal bones
occasional.notes: May be detected on physical exam
searchTerms: lump under skin near nose bones

rare.notes: Serious complication if cyst ruptures intracranially
searchTerms: brain membrane infection due to cyst

rare.notes: Rare but possible if brain tissue involved

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers if infected (e.g., CRP, ESR)
Normal routine blood tests in uncomplicated cases
imaging: CT scan showing well-defined cystic lesion along nasal dorsum
MRI demonstrating cyst characteristics and assessing intracranial extension
Possible bony remodeling or defect in nasal bones
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Histopathology showing keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with adnexal structures (hair follicles, sebaceous glands)
Presence of sinus tract lined by epithelium

distinguishingFeatures: No sinus tract or pit present
Histology shows glial tissue rather than dermoid elements
Pulsatile mass with possible CSF leak
Imaging shows herniation of brain tissue
Usually no sinus tract or intracranial extension

redFlags: Signs of intracranial extension on imaging
Neurological symptoms such as seizures or meningitis
references: Schaefer SD, et al. Nasal dermoid cysts: diagnosis and management. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2018.
Berenholz L, et al. Imaging of nasal dermoid cysts and sinuses. Radiographics. 2019.
